A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same k-NLPmeans/k-LLMmeans research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions and relocations.

before.justification: Sections 5–7 report original static and streaming clustering experiments and a StackExchange case study. Appendix B includes experimental results and standard deviations.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds BERTopic comparisons, cluster-count and sampling sensitivity results, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4, Equations 1–4, and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same summarization, re-embedding, assignment, and mini-batch updates. BERTopic embeddings and alternative samplers are additional experimental configurations; no revised core algorithm is specified.

E1.justification: The quantitative datasets, tasks, streaming years, and original case-study coverage are unchanged. Appendix E.7 newly presents multilingual/code-mixed failures, but their provenance and whether they extend the evaluated data are unspecified. Appendix A.1 still specifies English-only MASSIVE, leaving an actual expansion of language coverage unresolved.

E2.justification: BERTopic, previously only discussed in related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 1 and 3, with corresponding appendix tables. BERTopic-based applications of both proposed methods are also compared. The existing classical baselines, ClusterLLM, IDAS, and LLMEdgeRefine remain.

E3.justification: Added experiments use BERTopic-derived embeddings, vary k by ±10% and ±20%, and compare k-means++, random, nearest-centroid, and farthest-point sampling. Existing principal settings remain. The retained prompt experiment is ambiguously labeled FS-multiple in v4 Table 10 but FS-single in Appendix B.2.2, so an actual setting change there is unestablished.

E4.justification: V3's prompt and summary-length sensitivity analysis is retained as v4 Table 10. V4 substantially broadens analysis with cluster-count sensitivity (Table 9), representative-document sampling comparisons (Table 11), and seven qualitative failure cases examining summary fidelity and interpretability (Appendix E).

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds for proposed-method settings and streaming experiments, ten for traditional baselines, and appendix reporting of means and standard deviations. V4 extends the same uncertainty-reporting practice to added results without introducing new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Earlier numerical entries are retained, including v3 Table 9's scores in v4 Table 10. Substantial new results cover BERTopic configurations, k sensitivity, sampling, and qualitative failures. For example, v4 Table 1 adds BANK77 ACC values of 71.2 for BERTopic, 76.0 for BERTopic+kNLPmeans, and 75.7 for BERTopic+kLLMmeans; these are new configurations, not same-setting version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: The clustering objectives, centroid equations, and mathematical reasoning are retained, with no added theorem or proof. New Appendix C explains standard ACC and NMI formulas already used in v3; it does not establish a new metric or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, four listed contributions, and concluding contribution statements remain substantially unchanged. V4 adds an introductory qualification that the goal is improvement over k-means-style methods with interpretability and scalability, rather than strict dominance over every clustering algorithm.

C2.justification: V4 expands v3's brief limitations into detailed explanations of prompt echoing, hallucinated details, excessive compression, generic summaries, minority-topic omission, misleading emphasis, and multilingual drift. Appendix E discusses mitigations and the brevity–specificity and single-prototype tradeoffs. Section 5.1 also adds interpretations concerning BERTopic compatibility and robustness to k and sampling choices.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly identifies sklearn's NMI implementation and Hungarian matching for ACC. The reproducibility statement changes its code-access pointer from the named GitHub repository to an anonymized 4open.science repository. Existing hardware, runtime, cost, and principal hyperparameter disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The same 74 cited works are retained; bibliographic corrections and publication updates do not add research coverage. V4 nevertheless expands positioning relative to BERTopic by presenting the proposed methods as complementary improvements to its embeddings, beyond v3's brief related-work description.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering remain intact. V4 adds a goal qualification and results summary, subdivides Appendix B.2, inserts a metrics appendix, moves Algorithms from Appendix C to D, and adds the failure-analysis appendix. These are localized structural and explanatory extensions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The displays expand substantially: Tables 1, 3, 5, and 7 gain BERTopic blocks; new Tables 9 and 11 present sensitivity analyses; Appendix E adds seven paired snippet/summary displays. Original figures remain, with an expanded Figure 1 caption. The retained algorithms move from a shared page to separate pages interleaved with failure analysis.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the added baseline comparisons, sensitivity tests, explicit metric implementation, and concrete failure cases improve empirical scrutiny and understanding of limitations. The gain is tempered by unclear setup details and overgeneralized interpretations: Table 1's GoEmo ACC is 18.2 for BERTopic versus 17.4/17.7 for its hybrids, despite the claim of consistent improvement. Table 10 also introduces an FS-single/FS-multiple inconsistency. The net improvement is useful but limited.
